items.title: Toward detection of heart failure: development of a sensitive fluorescent kit for clinical sST2 detection.
items.abstract: Heart failure, the terminal stage of various cardiovascular diseases, typically presents with subtle early symptoms that are difficult to detect. Consequently, developing fast and accurate diagnostic tools is essential for effective early diagnosis and disease management. Soluble suppression of tumorigenicity 2 (sST2) is recognized as a valuable biomarker for predicting disease severity and mortality in cardiovascular disease, making it a promising target for developing a detection kit for early heart failure diagnosis. Recently, the CRISPR-Cas12a system has been increasingly used for quick and sensitive nucleic acid detection. However, its application in protein detection remains limited. In this study, we combined nanotechnology-mediated protein capture with the CRISPR-Cas12a system and developed a fluorescence-based method for rapid and sensitive detection of sST2. The presence of sST2 triggers the formation of a ternary complex, which can activate the trans -cleavage activity of Cas12a, resulting in cleavage of the response DNA single strand and the production of a fluorescent signal. Importantly, when tested on serum samples, this method can effectively distinguish patients with heart failure from healthy controls. This method offers a promising alternative to traditional enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs), with potential advantages in operational simplicity and detection speed. Therefore, this innovative fluorescence-based sST2 detection technique has significant potential for the clinical diagnosis of heart failure.

items.title: Effectiveness of Radiofrequency Renal Denervation in the United States: Six-Month Primary End Point Results From the SPYRAL AFFIRM Study.
items.abstract: Radiofrequency renal denervation (RDN) is a guideline-recommended therapy for uncontrolled hypertension. SPYRAL AFFIRM is a single-arm, postapproval study assessing the efficacy and safety of radiofrequency RDN using the Symplicity Spyral catheter. We report the 6-month primary end point results in the SPYRAL AFFIRM US population. Enrolled patients had an office systolic/diastolic blood pressure (BP) ≥140/90 mm Hg and a home systolic BP ≥135 mm Hg. Patients with type 1 diabetes, poorly controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c >8.0%), or an estimated glomerular filtration rate 2 were excluded. The primary end point was the 6-month change in office systolic BP from baseline compared with a prespecified performance goal (-6.0 mm Hg). Among 594 patients treated in the AFFIRM study from 73 US clinical sites, baseline clinical characteristics included: mean (±SD) age, 57±12 years; female, 45%; African American, 27%; Hispanic, 11%; type 2 diabetes, 19%; and mean estimated glomerular filtration rate, 79±20 mL/min per 1.73m 2 . Baseline systolic/diastolic office, home, and 24-hour ambulatory BP (mm Hg) were 169±21/106±13, 158±17/101±13, and 151±18/96±13, respectively. Patients were prescribed an average of 3.6±2.0 antihypertensive medications at baseline that remained unchanged through 6 months. Six months after RDN, the change in systolic BP (mm Hg) was -18.2±22.0, -9.4±13.8, and -9.7±16.8 for office, home, and 24-hour ambulatory measures, respectively ( P <0.001 compared with baseline). Adverse clinical events through 6 months were uncommon. In this US postapproval study, the primary end point was met with significant BP reductions following radiofrequency RDN consistent across different measures. In a broader patient population with uncontrolled hypertension, these results reaffirm the safety and efficacy of radiofrequency RDN. URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT05198674.

items.title: Transcutaneous Pacing in the Prehospital Setting - A Retrospective Cohort Study of Electrical Capture.
items.abstract: Transcutaneous pacing (TCP) treats hemodynamically unstable bradycardia refractory to pharmacologic management. Effective TCP requires electrical and mechanical capture to augment perfusion. Little is known about prehospital TCP and capture incidence. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of patients treated with prehospital TCP by an emergency medical services agency between 2017 and 2024. Continuous ECG recordings from cardiac monitors were reviewed. Electrical capture was the primary outcome, defined as a widened QRS with a distinct T wave following a TCP spike. Secondary measures included capture duration, clinician-verbalized pulse during pacing, plethysmograph waveform alignment, and changes in systolic blood pressure (SBP), pulse oximetry, and end-tidal carbon dioxide. Fifty-six patients received attempted TCP. Median age was 70 years (interquartile range [IQR] 58-85), and 34% were female. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) was administered in 59% of patients. Electrical capture was achieved in 18 patients (32%). Among patients who achieved electrical capture, complete capture occurred a mean of 27.2% (standard deviation 30.5%) of attempted pacing duration. The median SBP change was +22.0 (IQR: -2-82) mmHg in patients with electrical capture and 0.0 (IQR: -29-7) mmHg in those with only rare-to-absent capture ( p  = 0.031). During TCP, clinicians verbalized a palpable pulse 26 times across 19 patients. Only 4 instances (15%) coincided with electrical capture. Electrical capture during prehospital TCP occurred in a minority of patients and was often intermittent. Prehospital identification of mechanical capture using routine clinical indicators was difficult and unreliable. Future work should standardize capture definitions and physiologic measurements to determine when TCP produces clinically meaningful perfusion.

items.title: BAG3 genetic variant is associated with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction phenotypes.
items.abstract: Genetic variations are involved in determining heart failure (HF) phenotypes. While variants within the BAG3 gene have been associated with HF in European populations, the impact of specific single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) within the BAG3 gene in determining phenotypes of HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) in Southeast Asian populations is unknown. Therefore, in this study, we identified BAG3 SNPs and investigated their biological and clinical relevance in determining HFpEF phenotypes among an Indonesian HFpEF cohort. We conducted a study involving 36 patients with HFpEF and 30 healthy individuals. We detected the presence of rs196326 and rs2240777 SNPs in our cohort. However, the rs2234962 polymorphism, which has been associated with HF and cardiomyopathy in Western populations, was absent in our Indonesian cohort. We found that the rs196326 SNP was significantly associated with relative wall thickness (RWT), with patients carrying the CG genotype displayed significantly lower RWT. Additionally, the rs196326 CG/GG genotypes were correlated with higher serum N-terminal pro B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) and lower Caspase-3 levels. Our study showed that the BAG3 rs196326 polymorphism was significantly associated with HFpEF phenotypes in the Indonesian population. This highlights the importance of identifying population-specific as genetic markers of disease severity.

items.title: Complaint Driven Clinical Guidance and ICD Chapter Suggestion: An AI-Based Text Classification Tool.
items.abstract: Accurate routing of patients to appropriate clinical departments is essential for timely diagnosis, effective treatment, and efficient use of hospital resources. However, hospital statistics and feedback from patients and healthcare staff indicate that many patients select clinics that are not appropriate for their presenting complaints. This mismatch unnecessarily occupies appointment slots, limits access to appropriate care, and increases the operational burden on healthcare systems. To address this problem, a complaint-driven clinical guidance framework was developed to map patient complaints to suitable clinical departments and corresponding International Classification of Diseases (ICD) chapters. A 7-year electronic health record dataset comprising 1,795,645 patient complaints was used to train and evaluate conventional machine learning algorithms and BERT-based language models. The final classification tasks included 15 clinical departments for department recommendation and 12 ICD chapters for suggestion. For clinical department recommendation, Turkish BERT achieved the best performance, with a mean accuracy of 92.02%, precision of 92.91%, and F1-score of 92.08%. McNemar's test confirmed that its improvement over multilingual BERT-based alternatives was statistically significant. Error analysis indicated that most department-level misclassifications occurred between clinically related or symptomatically overlapping departments, including Internal Medicine-Cardiology, Neurosurgery and Physical Therapy, and Cardiovascular Surgery-Cardiology. For ICD chapter suggestion, Turkish BERT achieved the best performance among the evaluated models, with a top-1 accuracy of 66.7%, top-3 accuracy of 82.9%, top-5 accuracy of 85.4%. Although exact ICD chapter prediction remained challenging, the substantially higher top-3 and top-5 accuracies indicate that the model may be useful for generating ranked candidate ICD chapters. Confusion analysis showed that errors were mainly concentrated between clinically overlapping ICD chapters, particularly neoplasms/blood and immune disorders, endocrine/metabolic diseases, circulatory system diseases, and symptom-based chapters. These findings suggest that artificial intelligence-based systems can effectively support clinical department recommendation to improve hospital workflow efficiency, whereas ICD chapter suggestion may serve as a preliminary ranked decision-support tool.

items.title: Extracellular Matrix Stiffness Regulates Mechanical-Metabolic Coupling in Tumors: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities.
items.abstract: The extracellular matrix (ECM) stiffening in the tumor microenvironment (TME) is an important physical characteristic of solid tumors and can serve as an active signaling hub that regulates the biological behavior of tumors. Abnormal deposition, cross-linking, and remodeling of collagen not only alter the mechanical properties and structure of tissues but also convert mechanical stimuli into intracellular signals through mechanosensitive ion channels such as integrin-FAK, Hippo-YAP/TAZ, Piezo1/2, and Transient receptor potential vanilloid subtype 4 (TRPV4), thereby reprogramming tumor cell metabolism, including enhancing the Warburg effect, lipid synthesis, and glutamine catabolism, forming a malignant cycle of "matrix stiffening - metabolic reprogramming" that promotes tumor progression and treatment tolerance. Mechanical signals can also create an immunosuppressive TME by restricting CD8 + T-cell infiltration and promoting tumor-associated macrophage polarization toward an M2-like state. Metabolites generated by reprogrammed cells, including lactate, can further remodel and stiffen the ECM, creating a positive-feedback loop. Genetic and epigenetic heterogeneity, hypoxia, nutrient availability, and oncogenic signaling may uncouple mechanical regulation from metabolic output and complicate therapeutic targeting. Non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) add a regulatory layer that may connect mechanotransduction with metabolic plasticity and immune remodeling, although their effects remain context dependent. This review integrates the existing evidence on the regulation of tumor metabolism and immune microenvironment by ECM mechanical signals, focuses on summarizing the key mechanical sensing pathways, feedback mechanisms, and therapeutic targets, and proposes research directions for precisely identifying key regulatory nodes of the mechanical-metabolic axis by combining spatial omics, metabolic flux analysis, and mechanical imaging techniques, providing a conceptual framework for developing novel therapeutic strategies targeting the biomechanical processes of tumors.

items.title: Detection of RET fusion in late-line treatment of NSCLC followed by long-term disease control with selpercatinib.
items.abstract: RET gene fusions represent a rare but clinically relevant genetic alteration in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), particularly in adenocarcinoma, with a prevalence of approximately 1-2%. Identification of this driver mutation has enabled the development of selective RET tyrosine kinase inhibitors, which significantly improve treatment outcomes in these patients. Molecular testing, including detection of RET fusions, is currently a standard component of the diagnostic algorithm for advanced NSCLC. We present the case of a 55-year-old female non-smoker diagnosed with metastatic lung adenocarcinoma with central nervous system (CNS) involvement. Initial molecular testing revealed no alterations in EGFR, ALK, or ROS1, and PD-L1 expression was negative. The patient underwent hippocampus-avoiding whole-brain radiotherapy followed by three lines of systemic treatment including chemotherapy and immunotherapy. Upon disease progression, next--generation sequencing analysis of a rebiopsy specimen obtained from a supraclavicular metastasis identified a RET gene fusion. Based on this finding, treatment with selpercatinib was initiated in January 2022 as the fourth-line therapy. Treatment resulted in a rapid and profound response, including complete regression of CNS metastases. Therapy was well tolerated; initial hepatotoxicity was successfully managed by dose reduction. The patient has remained on RET inhibitor therapy for nearly 4 years with sustained disease control. This case highlights the importance of comprehensive molecular testing in patients with advanced NSCLC. Identification of RET fusion may enable the use of highly effective targeted therapy even after failure of multiple lines of systemic treatment.

items.title: Long term response to immunotherapy in a patient with low PD-L1 expression, high tumor mutational burden, and STK11 mutation.
items.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors are an integral part of the treatment of a wide range of malignancies, including non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). With the expanding indications for immunotherapy in recent years, clinical experience has increased exponentially, encompassing both its therapeutic efficacy and associated adverse events. In an effort to rationalize the use of immunotherapy, considerable attention is currently focused on identification of predictive biomarkers that would allow for more precise selection of patients likely to benefit from this treatment. The authors present a case report of a patient with lung adenocarcinoma characterized by low PD-L1 expression, high tumor mutational burden (37 muts/Mb), and an STK11 mutation. This represents a combination of two predictors of poor response to immunotherapy (low PD-L1 expression and STK11 mutation) along with a high tumor mutational burden, which is conversely considered a predictor of sensitivity to immunotherapy. The patient was treated according to the currently well-established standard of first-line systemic therapy, consisting of pembrolizumab in combination with chemotherapy. This treatment resulted in a durable response, which given its current duration, may be considered sustained with minimal adverse effects. Immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy, as illustrated by this case, may lead to durable responses and prolonged survival even in patients with unfavorable predictive biomarkers. Within the decision-making algorithm prior to initiation of systemic therapy in metastatic NSCLC, it is beneficial to perform a comprehensive and readily available predictive and molecular analysis.

items.title: Calreticulin exposure is a critical mediator of high-dose vitamin C-induced immune surveillance in the tumor microenvironment.
items.abstract: High-dose vitamin C (vitC) has shown superior anticancer activity in immunocompetent compared with immunodeficient mice, suggesting an immunodependent mechanism of action. Because high-dose vitC generates substantial reactive oxygen species (ROS), we hypothesized that ROS could induce immunogenic cell death (ICD), a regulated form of cell death characterized by the release of damage-associated molecular patterns (DAMPs) that enhance antigen presentation and promote antitumor immunity. Spatial transcriptomic and immunofluorescence analyses were performed on breast and colon tumors from mice treated with high-dose vitC to quantify oxidative stress, DAMP mobilization, and immune cell infiltration. To dissect the functional role of ROS and ICD, mice were treated with high-dose vitC in combination with the antioxidant N-acetylcysteine or an antibody blocking calreticulin (an early DAMP essential for ICD induction). VitC treatment caused marked oxidative stress in tumors from both immunocompetent and immunocompromised mice; however, tumor growth inhibition occurred exclusively in immunocompetent animals. High-dose vitC triggered ROS-dependent exposure and release of the DAMPs calreticulin and HMGB1, respectively. This was accompanied by substantial remodeling of the tumor microenvironment, including increased infiltration of cytotoxic CD8⁺ T cells and natural killer cells, and a reduction in immunosuppressive regulatory T cells. Blocking calreticulin effectively disrupted the ICD cascade, prevented immune microenvironment remodeling, and completely abrogated the antitumor efficacy of vitC. Collectively, our study indicates that high-dose vitC promotes ICD by mobilizing calreticulin and HMGB1, and that calreticulin is a determinant of its immune-mediated antitumor activity. Implications: vitC induces ICD, supporting its use as an adjuvant to anticancer immunotherapy.

items.title: CDH3-directed immunotherapy targets basal-like hormone receptor negative prostate cancer and breast cancer.
items.abstract: Basal-like double-negative prostate cancer (DNPC) and triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) are aggressive tumors with few targeted treatment options, raising the question of whether a shared, druggable cell-surface antigen can be leveraged for effective immunotherapy. Here, we integrated analyses of independent bulk and single-cell transcriptomic datasets with mechanistic and preclinical therapeutic studies to evaluate CDH3 (P-cadherin) as a candidate target in basal-like disease. CDH3 expression was consistently enriched in basal-like subtypes across prostate and breast cancer cohorts and was preferentially expressed in basal epithelial tumor compartments. Mechanistically, CDH3 expression was governed by a YAP1-WNT5A/ROR2 signaling axis, linking basal subtype gene expression to non-canonical Wnt signaling. To exploit this target, we evaluated both a CDH3-directed antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) and CDH3-specific chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cells. The ADC exhibited antigen-dependent internalization and cytotoxicity in vitro and reduced metastatic tumor burden in vivo. CDH3 CAR-T cells showed antigen-specific activation and tumor cell killing in vitro and improved tumor control and survival in metastatic prostate and breast cancer xenograft models, with additional benefit when combined with PD-1 blockade (nivolumab). Together, these findings establish CDH3 as a clinically relevant and therapeutically actionable target and support CDH3-directed ADC and CAR-T strategies for aggressive, basal-like DNPC and TNBC.

items.title: Hepatitis C Treatment Access With Implementation of an Antenatal Linkage-to-Care Bundle.
items.abstract: To evaluate a health system-wide quality-improvement bundle (HALT-C [hepatitis C antenatal linkage-to-care]) on its ability to integrate proactive patient identification, care coordination, and treatment timing options on direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum. We implemented our quality-improvement initiative at a large midwestern health system and evaluated its effect by comparing outcomes among eligible pregnancies identified preimplementation (December 1, 2021-May 31, 2023) with those identified postimplementation (March 1, 2024-August 31, 2025). Eligible patients were aged at least 18 years, with detectable hepatitis C virus RNA and at least one encounter in the health system before 35 weeks of gestation. The primary outcome was the percentage of patients prescribed direct-acting antivirals by 6 months postpartum. Secondary outcomes included linkage to care, the treatment timing decision, treatment completion, sustained virologic response (SVR), infant screening, and perinatal transmission. Comparison of antenatal initiation of treatment and postpartum initiation of treatment was also performed. We identified 62 bundle-eligible pregnancies in the preimplementation period and identified 35 in the postimplementation period. Direct-acting antiviral prescription by 6 months postpartum increased from 48.4% to 77.1% (P=.009); treatment completion improved from 21.0% to 54.3% (P=.001). Treatment increases were greatest among patients who delivered regionally, rather than at the main hospital, with an increase in direct-acting antiviral prescription rates of 14.3% to 72.7% (P<.001). Thirty of 35 individuals identified postimplementation were successfully linked to care, and 75.0% of clinic attendees preferred antenatal treatment over postpartum treatment. Known treatment completion and SVR increased from 21.0% to 54.3% (P=.001). Those treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment than those who deferred postpartum (92.3% vs 45.5%; P=.02). Infant screening and perinatal transmission rates did not change; however, no perinatal transmissions occurred among infants where treatment occurred antenatally. The HALT-C bundle was associated with significantly improved direct-acting antiviral receipt across a regional health system. Most patients preferred treatment during pregnancy. Patients treated antenatally were twice as likely to complete treatment, highlighting pregnancy as an important opportunity to initiate curative therapy.

items.title: PIVKA-II and hematological parameters in hepatocellular carcinoma and non-malignant chronic liver disease: A case-control biomarker comparison in a hepatitis-endemic population.
items.abstract: Early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains challenging in hepatitis-endemic settings such as Pakistan, where surveillance commonly relies on ultrasonography and alpha-fetoprotein (AFP), both of which have limited sensitivity for early-stage disease. This study evaluated the diagnostic performance of serum Protein Induced by Vitamin K Absence or Antagonist-II (PIVKA-II), complete blood count (CBC) parameters, and CBC-derived hematological indices for discriminating HCC from non-malignant chronic liver disease (CLD). We conducted a case-control biomarker study involving 160 adults with CLD at Liaquat University Hospital, Sindh, Pakistan, between October 2025 and March 2026, including 74 patients with established HCC and 86 with non-malignant CLD. Serum PIVKA-II was measured using electrochemiluminescence immunoassay. CBC-derived neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, and red cell distribution width-to-platelet ratio were calculated. Between-group differences were assessed using non-parametric methods, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis evaluated discriminatory performance. Benjamini-Hochberg correction was applied to prespecified families of multiple comparisons. PIVKA-II demonstrated the strongest discriminatory performance, with an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.753 (95% CI, 0.670-0.827). At a cutoff of >82.1 mAU/mL, sensitivity was 86.4% and specificity was 56.0%. Platelet count (AUC, 0.642) and the RDW-to-platelet ratio (AUC, 0.638) also demonstrated significant between-group differences that remained significant after false discovery rate correction, although their discriminatory performance was modest. PIVKA-II discrimination was substantially higher among patients with vascular invasion (AUC, 0.853) and advanced BCLC stage C/D disease (AUC, 0.853) than among those with early/intermediate BCLC A/B disease (AUC, 0.571). A combined model incorporating PIVKA-II, lymphocyte percentage, and platelet count yielded an AUC of 0.784, but did not significantly improve discrimination compared with PIVKA-II alone (p = 0.166). Bootstrap validation showed minimal optimism in the overall AUC; however, the optimal PIVKA-II cutoff demonstrated substantial variability, with a 95% percentile range of 58.7-715.8 mAU/mL. This was corroborated by an independent 10-fold cross-validation analysis, which yielded a comparable mean AUC of 0.751 for PIVKA-II (optimism = +0.002). PIVKA-II demonstrated fair diagnostic discrimination between HCC and non-malignant CLD, with relatively high sensitivity but limited specificity. Its substantially lower performance in early/intermediate-stage disease and the marked instability of the optimal cutoff indicate that PIVKA-II should be considered a complementary biomarker rather than a standalone diagnostic test. Larger multicenter studies with standardized control populations and independent external validation are needed to establish robust population-specific thresholds and determine the incremental clinical value of combining PIVKA-II with hematological parameters.

items.title: Development and Pilot-Testing of an Educational Intervention to Promote Concurrent Hepatitis C Virus and Colorectal Cancer Screening Behaviors Among Community Health Clinic Patients.
items.abstract: IntroductionWe aimed to develop an educational intervention booklet for promoting hepatitis C virus (HCV) and colorectal cancer (CRC) screening; and to assess intervention satisfaction, screening intentions, and changes in individuals' HCV/CRC knowledge and health beliefs in a pilot test of the educational booklet.MethodsWe developed a preliminary HCV/CRC education booklet informed by the Preventive Health Model with input from a community advisory board. During Study 1, feedback about the booklet was gathered through qualitative methods using individual interviews (n=13) with participants recruited from two community health centers. Interview questions addressed education material attraction, clarity, preferred delivery channels, and ability to promote action. Rapid qualitative analysis was utilized, and the booklet was revised based on feedback. For the pilot trial (Study 2), 26 participants were recruited, completed baseline quantitative surveys assessing HCV/CRC knowledge and health beliefs, and were provided the booklet to review. Approximately 7-14 days later, participants (n=19) completed a follow-up survey which assessed knowledge, health beliefs, screening intentions, and intervention satisfaction, which were examined using descriptive statistics.ResultsIn Study 1, a theory-informed booklet was produced and utilized in Study 2. From baseline to follow-up in Study 2, there was an increase in participants' objective CRC/HCV knowledge ( p p <0.005, respectively) and there were changes in several CRC/HCV health beliefs. Most participants agreed that they learned new information (90%), and that the information was easy to follow (89.5%) and understand (89.5%). All participants (100%) reported that the information was very/somewhat helpful. Participants' reported intentions to complete CRC screening and HCV screening in the next 6 months were 71% and 40%, respectively.ConclusionFindings suggest that the team was able to produce a theory-informed educational intervention booklet which led to changes in health beliefs and knowledge.Practice ImplicationsBundling education about multiple cancer screening behaviors is feasible.

items.title: Liver concentrations of JNJ-73763989 siRNA triggers in patients with chronic hepatitis B (CHB): The INSIGHT study panel 3 results.
items.abstract: BackgroundJNJ-73763989 is a 2:1 combination of 2 N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc)-conjugated short interfering RNAs (siRNA) targeting the S (daplusiran) and X (tomligisiran) regions of the hepatitis B virus genome. In phase 2b studies, 48 weeks of JNJ-73763989-based combination treatments led to dose-dependent reductions in viral markers, including hepatitis B surface antigen. The objective of the INSIGHT study Panel 3 was to quantify intrahepatic concentrations of the siRNAs in human livers during and after treatment.MethodsIn the open-label, single-arm, single-center study, participants with chronic hepatitis B received 48 weeks of treatment with JNJ-73763989 200 mg every 4 weeks and nucleos(t)ide analog, with optional pegylated interferon α2a 180 µg weekly added after Treatment Week (TW) 40. Core liver biopsies were collected at TW12, TW40, and at Follow-up Week (FUW) 24.ResultsLiver biopsies were available from all 4 participants at TW12 and from 3 at TW40 and FUW24. Between TW12 and TW40, liver concentrations of daplusiran and tomligisiran increased 1.5- to 2.6-fold, consistent with intrahepatic accumulation. Twenty-eight weeks after the last injection of JNJ-73763989, the triggers were still measurable in 2 of 3 participants with 4.5- to 15-fold reduced concentrations from peak levels; the estimated liver half-life ranged from approximately 2.9 to 16.1 weeks.ConclusionsIn this first study to assess liver concentrations of GalNAc-siRNA in humans with sequential biopsies, long persistence of JNJ-73763989 triggers in human livers may partially explain the prolonged suppressive effect on viral parameters observed in phase 2 studies.

items.title: Taurine bolsters adoptive T cell therapy efficacy against hepatocellular carcinoma by reprogramming T cell function.
items.abstract: Adoptive T cell therapy for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is limited by the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, which impairs T-cell function. Overcoming this immunosuppression and restoring T-cell functionality are crucial for improving therapeutic efficacy. Here, we investigated the role of taurine in regulating alpha-fetoprotein (AFP)-specific T-cell receptor-engineered T cells (TCR-T) function. Metabolomic profiling revealed that intracellular taurine levels declined during the early phase of T-cell activation, while expression of the taurine transporter SLC6A6 increased over time. In addition, taurine abundance was lower in HCC tissues than in normal liver tissues in vivo, suggesting that taurine availability is reduced during both T-cell activation and tumor progression. Functionally, taurine supplementation enhanced the cytotoxic activity, persistence, and intratumoral infiltration of AFP-specific TCR-T, while reducing exhaustion and apoptosis after repetitive tumor stimulation. In contrast, taurine-limited conditions impaired T-cell proliferation and survival, attenuated antitumor activity in vitro and in vivo, and promoted an exhaustion-prone phenotype. Taurine supplementation also partially restored the function of β-alanine-preconditioned T cells. Mechanistically, transcriptomic and proteomic analyses identified PI3K-AKT signaling as a key pathway associated with taurine-mediated T-cell regulation. Taurine-limited T cells showed reduced AKT phosphorylation and developed a metabolically stressed state characterized by increased mitochondrial respiration, glycolytic activity, reactive oxygen species production and mitochondrial structural abnormalities during activation. Together, these findings identify taurine availability as an important metabolic regulator of engineered T-cell fitness and support taurine-based metabolic conditioning as a potential strategy to improve TCR-T therapy for HCC.

items.title: Longitudinal timepoint assessment of patient-reported clinical disease activity in ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease: suitability of a rapid Patient-Reported Outcome 2 (PRO-2) assessment.
items.abstract: Patient-reported outcomes (PRO) are essential for monitoring disease activity and treatment response in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). The conventional PRO-2 requires several days of prospective symptom recording, increasing participant burden and attrition in longitudinal research. We evaluated whether a "rapid PRO-2", using 2 days of data collected retrospectively and prospectively in a single day, could serve as a reliable and pragmatic alternative to a 4-day PRO-2. Using data from the ongoing IBD-RESPONSE cohort (n = 684 Crohn's disease [CD]; n = 548 ulcerative colitis [UC]), we compared 4-day PRO-2 and rapid PRO-2 scores at baseline and 14 weeks post-therapy to assess disease activity, clinical (non) response and remission. At baseline, 87.1% (596/684) of CD and 88.7% (486/548) of UC patients remained in the same active/inactive disease activity category (Cohen's kappa: CD 0.715; UC 0.762; both P < .001). At week 14, 77% (CD; 195/252) and 83.1% (UC; 193/232) remained in the same non-response/response/remission category (Cohen's kappa: CD 0.653; UC 0.743; both P < .001). Discrepancies mainly involved adjacent category shifts (ie, between response and remission, or non-response and response), with minimal re-classification between remission and non-response (n = 7 CD and n = 2 UC). Greater symptom variability across the 4 days increased the likelihood of switching between remission and non-response (odds ratio [95% confidence interval], CD 5.0 [3.65-6.85]; UC 7.8 [5.6-11.0], both P < .001). Responsiveness to clinical change was comparable between instruments. The rapid PRO-2 retains essential symptom data and demonstrates strong agreement with the 4-day PRO-2, offering an alternative in longitudinal studies to minimize burden and attrition.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Arc Geometrical Configurations and Jaw Tracking for Peripheral Low-Dose Bath in Whole Breast VMAT.
items.abstract: IntroductionMinimizing low-dose radiation spillage to surrounding organs at risk (OARs) is a critical consideration in whole breast irradiation (WBI) using volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT). While VMAT improves dose conformity and delivery efficiency, its continuous arc delivery may increase the "low-dose bath" in normal tissues. This study compared the dosimetric impact of arc geometry and jaw tracking under controlled planning conditions to characterize their effects on low-dose exposure.MethodsIn this retrospective dosimetric study, VMAT plans were generated for 30 breast cancer patients (15 left-sided and 15 right-sided). Four arc configurations were evaluated: conventional-arc VMAT (two and four arcs), tangential-arc VMAT (TA-VMAT), and hybrid-arc VMAT (HA-VMAT). Each configuration was planned with and without jaw tracking using identical objectives. Dose-volume histogram (DVH) parameters were analyzed for the planning target volume (PTV) and OARs, including the ipsilateral/contralateral lungs, heart, left anterior descending coronary artery (LAD), liver, and contralateral breast.ResultsAll techniques achieved comparable target coverage. Arc configuration substantially affected OAR dose distribution. Compared with conventional-arc VMAT, TA-VMAT reduced contralateral lung and breast exposure by 60-70%, while HA-VMAT yielded intermediate results. Notably, tangential arc restriction increased ipsilateral lung dose, particularly in right-sided cases, and increased LAD dose in left-sided cases. Jaw tracking provided additional dose reductions in selected OAR metrics, although the magnitude and statistical significance of these changes varied across arc configurations.ConclusionsThe findings suggest that peripheral low-dose exposure in whole-breast VMAT is influenced by arc configuration, while jaw tracking may provide additional dose reduction in selected OAR metrics. Considering both beam geometry and delivery-level leakage control may help reduce unnecessary OAR exposure.

items.title: Dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI and tumor microenvironment in hepatocellular carcinoma: exploratory analysis of CD3 + TILs, PD-L1, and glypican-3.
items.abstract: Dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the clinical diagnostic standard in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but its association with the tumor microenvironment is not fully characterized. In this study, we investigated correlations between DCE-MRI parameters and immunohistochemistry features of HCC. Forty patients, six women and 34 men aged 61.5 ± 10.1 years (mean ± standard deviation) with histologically confirmed HCC were included. DCE-MRI with Gd-EOB-DTPA was performed before surgery, and quantitative parameters were calculated to reflect arterial wash-in, portal venous wash-out and hepatobiliary uptake. Pathological specimens were analyzed for programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1), glypican-3, CD3+ tumor- and stromal-infiltrating lymphocytes, CD68 and CD34. CD3+ stromal lymphocytes infiltration was inversely correlated with the arterial wash-in (r = -0.47; adjusted p-value = 0.025) and several post-arterial parameters. For the other TME components, only exploratory correlations were identified, none of which were statistically significant after adjustment for multiple testing. CD3+ tumoral infiltration lymphocytes with arterial wash-in (r = -0.35) and transitional phase relative signal intensity (SI) (r = 0.35). Native SI was inversely correlated with PD-L1 (r = -0.32). Difference in SI between the transitional and portal phase correlated with glypican-3 expression (r = 0.32). DCE-MRI shows a moderate association with stromal infiltrating lymphocytes (CD3⁺ SIL) in HCC. Associations with other components of the TME, including tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (CD3⁺ TIL), PD-L1 and Glypican-3 expression, were observed at uncorrected thresholds, but did not remain statistically significant after correction for multiple testing. Question DCE-MRI constitutes the cornerstone of HCC diagnosis. Is quantitative assessment of wash-in, wash-out and hepatobiliary uptake associated with non-invasive characterization of the TME? Findings CD3⁺ SIL were associated with tumor wash-in and wash-out parameters. Exploratory associations involving CD3⁺ TIL, PD-L1, and glypican-3 lost significance after multiple-testing adjustment. Relevance statement Quantitative DCE-MRI parameters may provide additional non-invasive information regarding tumor tissue characteristics and the tumor microenvironment of HCC.

items.title: Patient-specific biophysical AI-powered modeling for predicting RFA volumes in HCC.
items.abstract: To clinically evaluate a fully automated, artificial intelligence-powered, patient-specific biophysical model for predicting radiofrequency ablation (RFA) volumes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and to compare its performance with manufacturer-provided ablation estimates. This retrospective study included 96 RFA procedures in 65 HCC patients treated using a single ablation with a cluster needle. Tumors, needle position, and postablation zone were manually segmented on periprocedural computed tomography. Liver parenchyma and vascular structures were automatically extracted using deep learning. A graphics processing unit (GPU)-accelerated biophysical model simulated heat transfer, vascular heat-sink effects, and tissue necrosis using patient-specific anatomy and procedural data. Correlations between ablation volume manually segmented and clinical or anatomical parameters (ablation time, ablation tip temperature, tumor-capsule distance, vessel proximity, type, and diameter) were assessed. Model-predicted volumes were compared with ground truth and manufacturer estimates using relative volume difference (RVD) and volume similarity. Final ablation volumes showed wide variability (7.9-78.8 cm³) and were not correlated with any individual clinical or anatomical parameter (Pearson r - 0.02 to 0.29). Across 94 evaluable cases, simulated and ground-truth volumes were similar (p = 0.165), while manufacturer estimates significantly overestimated ablation volume (p < 0.001). The model achieved a median RVD of 0.39 (interquartile range 0.24-0.57), significantly lower than the manufacturer's algorithm (1.04; 0.64-1.61). Incorporating patient-specific ablation time further improved accuracy. Simulation was fast (0.45 s per second of ablation on GPU). A fully automated, patient-specific biophysical model substantially improves RFA ablation volume prediction in HCC compared with manufacturer approximations, supporting its potential role in personalized treatment planning and outcome standardization. Question In patients with hepatocellular carcinoma, can a fully automated, AI-powered, patient-specific biophysical model predict radiofrequency ablation volume more accurately than manufacturer-provided estimates? Findings A fully automated, AI-powered biophysical model integrating patient-specific anatomy and vasculature predicted RFA volume significantly better than manufacturer estimates (median relative volume difference (RVD) 0.39 versus 1.04). Relevance statement Accurate ablation volume prediction could support personalized radiofrequency ablation (RFA) planning, reduce reliance on operator experience, and standardize treatment margins in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), potentially improving local tumor control and reducing recurrence in cirrhotic patients undergoing thermal ablation.
